title: How a Hurricane Turns Warm Ocean Into a Storm
description: The engine, spin, eye and wind speed of a hurricane, from NOAA and NASA.
narration: What turns warm ocean water into a giant spinning storm? A hurricane works like an engine that runs on warm, moist air. As the warm air rises, it leaves an area of lower pressure below. Rising air cools, and its water vapour forms clouds. North of the equator they spin counterclockwise; south of it, clockwise. At the centre an eye forms, calm and clear. Once its sustained winds reach 74 miles per hour, the storm counts as a hurricane. On land they usually weaken, because the warm ocean no longer feeds them.

claims.quote: Tropical cyclones usually weaken when they hit land, because they are no longer being fed by the energy from the warm ocean waters.
